summary: Kenji Matsuo is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1973 to 1981 and served at Yamagata University from circa 1987 to 2020.
Kenji Shimada (1917–2000) worked in Sinology and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1938 to 1941 and later held a researcher post there from circa 1945 to 1981.

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University (2015–2016) and under supervisors Diwakar Acharya, Yuko Yokochi, and Peter Bisschop, as well as Somadeva Vasudeva, Andrey Klebanov, and Masato Fujii. He held a JSPS fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II (2019–2021).

Kenju Kasahara (1851–1883) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Oxford in 1879, and learned under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell between 1879 and 1882.
Kenjuro Yanagida (1893–1983) was a philosopher who studied at Yokohama National University and under Kitaro Nishida circa 1921–1924. He later held a post at Hirosaki University.
Kennard Lipman works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Herbert V. Günther and served as a sessional instructor at the University of Calgary.

Kenneth Adrian Raine Kennedy (1930–2014) specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of California, Berkeley from circa 1951 to 1962 and held a post at Cornell University from circa 1964 to 2005.
Kenneth Doo Young Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his doctorate at Columbia University under Ryuichi Abe and held a post at Stetson University, attested in 2007.

Kenneth G. Zysk specializes in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and Australian National University, holding posts at UCLA, Eastern Michigan University, the universities of Wisconsin-Madison and Toronto, and Copenhagen.

Kenneth J. Guest works in religious studies and Sinology. He studied at Columbia, Peking University, Union Theological Seminary, under Aloysius Pieris, and earned his PhD at the CUNY Graduate Center. He held posts at Hunter College and Baruch College.

Kenneth J. Saunders (1883–1937) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under W. D. C. Wagiswara. From circa 1921 to 1935, he served at the Pacific School of Religion and the University of California.

Kenneth K. Inada (1923–2011) specialized in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held posts at the University at Buffalo (attested 1983–1999), chaired the Numata Center (1996–1999), and chaired the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism until 1999.

Kenneth K. Tanaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at CSU, Stanford, IBS, Eastern Institute, University of Tokyo, and UC Berkeley. He held posts at IBS, UC Berkeley, Musashino University, and chaired the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism.
Kenneth R. Valpey is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held a post at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Kenneth Roy Norman (1925–2020) specialized in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Taunton School and Downing College, Cambridge, he served at the University of Cambridge (1955–1992) and as president of the Pali Text Society (1981–1994).

Kenneth de Burgh Codrington (1899–1986) was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist educated at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge, and Wadham College. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum (circa 1931–1948), University of London (circa 1948–1966), and University of Cincinnati.

Kenryo Minowa is a Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toho Kenkyukai, Aichi Gakuin University, University of Tokyo, and Rissho University, and became board chairman of the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies in 2023.
Kenryu T. Tsuji (1919–2004) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed his studies at Ryukoku University in 1938 and at the University of Toronto.

Kenryu Tsukinowa (1888–1969) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar educated at Bukkyo University. He held professorships at Koyasan, Seizan College, and Shuchiin University, and was named professor emeritus at Ryukoku University in 1956.

Kenryū Nishio is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate in literature at Otani University and became a professor emeritus at Hanazono University, attested in 2014.
